sections.content: You know the *indefinido* (A2 Unit 11), the *imperfecto* (A2 Unit 21), their contrast (A2 Unit 22), the *pluscuamperfecto* and *así que* (B1 Unit 1). Here you combine them to tell a problem at home: the *imperfecto* gives background, the *indefinido* advances the story, and *por eso* and *así que* show consequences.

items.spanish: Mientras dormíamos, una tubería se rompió y el agua empezó a salir.
items.english: While we were sleeping, a pipe broke and the water started coming out.

items.spanish: Había una fuga, así que llamamos al propietario inmediatamente.
items.english: There was a leak, so we called the landlord immediately.

items.spanish: El agua inundó parte de la cocina, por eso tuvimos que salir.
items.english: The water flooded part of the kitchen, so we had to leave.

items.spanish: Cuando llegó el técnico, ya habíamos cerrado la llave del agua.
items.english: When the technician arrived, we had already turned off the water.

sections.content: Use the *imperfecto* for the situation in progress, the *indefinido* for the event that changes it, and connectors to make the cause-and-consequence relationship explicit.
